security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, external reference links, and in-memory coordination examples. I confirmed the filesystem documentation examples because they show unsanitized path construction and non-atomic lock files that may be copied into production. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious hidden behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Filesystem coordination examples build file paths from identifiers such as key and workflow_id.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths under a fixed workspace root, reject path separators, and validate identifiers before writing files.

remediation.issue: The lock example checks for a file and then writes it in separate operations.
remediation.suggestion: Use atomic file creation, advisory locks, or a coordination service for shared agent locks.

remediation.issue: Checkpoint directory creation accepts a caller-provided path without boundary checks.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain checkpoint storage to an approved project directory and document required permissions.

content.value_statement: Complex AI work often exceeds one agent context or needs parallel specialists. This skill provides practical patterns for designing coordinated multi-agent systems.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical multi-agent patterns with trade-offs.
Guides context isolation through delegation, instruction passing, and shared state.
Describes weighted voting, debate protocols, and convergence checks for coordination.
Includes examples for direct message forwarding, handoffs, and request routing.
Compares LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI implementation approaches.
limitations: It is guidance material, not a complete runnable multi-agent framework.
Example code requires validation and hardening before production use.
External framework links may change after publication.
It does not automatically enforce security controls in generated systems.

use_cases.title: Plan a Complex AI Application
use_cases.description: Choose a supervisor, swarm, or hierarchy pattern for a product feature with multiple reasoning domains.

use_cases.title: Define Production Coordination Rules
use_cases.description: Create handoff, voting, retry, and circuit breaker rules for a team of specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Structure Parallel Research Workflows
use_cases.description: Separate research, analysis, validation, and writing tasks across agents with clear aggregation points.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent architecture for this task: [task]. Compare supervisor, swarm, and hierarchy patterns. Recommend one pattern and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Map Agent Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent plan for [project]. Define each agent, its context boundary, tools, inputs, outputs, and handoff rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Coordination Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed multi-agent workflow: [workflow]. Add voting, debate, retry, timeout, and circuit breaker controls where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Agent Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this multi-agent system for bottlenecks, divergence, error propagation, context leakage, and token cost. Recommend concrete design changes.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a multi-agent architecture for market research and report writing.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: supervisor. Agents: researcher, analyst, fact-checker, and writer. The supervisor assigns tasks and aggregates concise results.

output_examples.input: A team wants agents to solve an open-ended product investigation in parallel.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: swarm with explicit handoffs. Add convergence checks, maximum rounds, and direct response forwarding for final specialist answers.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs resilience guidance for an agent workflow.
output_examples.output: Suggested controls: output validation, weighted consensus, retry limits, circuit breakers, checkpointing, and timeout rules for every agent handoff.

best_practices: Use multi-agent design when context isolation or true parallel work improves the result.
Define handoff contracts, output schemas, and termination rules before adding agents.
Validate agent outputs before passing them to downstream agents or users.
anti_patterns: Do not split work into agents only to mirror an organization chart.
Do not let all agents share full context when isolation is the main goal.
Do not rely on simple majority voting when agent quality differs.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when one agent cannot manage the context, tools, or parallel work needed for a task.

faq.question: Does this skill build a full framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, design patterns, and examples that you can adapt.

faq.question: Which platforms does it mention?
faq.answer: It references LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI as examples of multi-agent implementation approaches.

faq.question: Can it help with reliability?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers validation, retries, circuit breakers, checkpoints, and failure propagation risks.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review filesystem examples, path validation, lock safety, token cost, and all handoff boundaries.
